ui.title: Resources
ui.aiNote: This translation was written with the help of AI and has not yet been reviewed by a native speaker. The English version is the official one. Names, phone numbers and websites are shown as each organization publishes them.
ui.nowIntro: If you or a loved one is suffering from a mental health emergency, call or text 988 (Suicide and Crisis Lifeline). If someone is in immediate danger, call 911.
ui.c1Text: Call or text, 24 hours a day. Free and confidential.
ui.c2Text: Text with a volunteer crisis counselor, 24 hours a day. Free.
ui.c3Text: A free, confidential peer support helpline run by Naseeha, open 24 hours a day.
ui.dirIntro: Search by name or need, or narrow the list by what you need help with, type of help, community, or location. This directory is free and open to people of all backgrounds. The organizations listed are independent of The Shifa Institute, which provides education and community programming, not clinical treatment.
ui.emptyText: Try a shorter word, or clear the filters to see the full list. In an emergency, call or text 988.
ui.a1: Your insurance card if you have one, the days and times you are free, and a sentence or two about what you want help with. You do not need a diagnosis to call.
ui.q2: What can I ask a therapist or clinic?
ui.a2: You can ask what a session costs, whether they take your insurance or offer a sliding scale, whether they have worked with clients of your faith or background, and which languages they offer.
ui.q3: What if the first one is not a good fit?
ui.a3: That is common. You can try someone else. A directory in the list above lets you compare several providers before you choose.
ui.a4: Most helplines say they are confidential, and many let you stay anonymous. Each listing links to the organization's own website, where you can read its privacy rules before you call.
ui.q5: I am a student. Where do I start?
ui.a5: Your campus counseling center is usually free for enrolled students. Choose "Campus counseling" under Type of help to find the five universities with a chapter of Shifa.
ui.d1: A licensed professional who provides talk therapy. Therapists do not prescribe medication.
ui.d2: A medical doctor who can diagnose mental health conditions and prescribe medication.
ui.d3: A trained person at a survivor support organization who can explain your options, help you make a safety plan, and go with you to appointments. An advocate is not a lawyer or a therapist.
ui.d4: A fee that goes down based on your income. Ask about it if cost is a concern.
ui.d5: Sessions held by video or phone instead of in person.
ui.d6: A phone line for when you want to talk to someone but are not in crisis. Warmlines are often staffed by people who have lived through similar struggles.
ui.d7: Counseling and Psychological Services, the name many universities use for their student counseling center.
ui.report: Each listing shows the date it was last checked. A listing is not an endorsement, and details can change, so please confirm them with the organization. If you find something out of date, or know of a resource we should add, please email
ui.termsLink: Read the terms for this directory.

michigan-state-university-counseling-psy.d: Counseling and crisis support for MSU students, in person and virtual. Ongoing services are not available to students living outside Michigan.
michigan-state-university-counseling-psy.hours: Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; crisis counselors 24/7 by pressing 1

university-of-michigan-counseling-and-ps.d: Counseling and psychological services through University Health Service for University of Michigan Ann Arbor students, at the Michigan Union.
university-of-michigan-counseling-and-ps.hours: Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. (5 p.m. in spring/summer); Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

university-of-michigan-dearborn-counseli.d: Free counseling for current University of Michigan-Dearborn students, in person or remote, with after-hours phone access to a licensed clinician.
university-of-michigan-dearborn-counseli.hours: Office Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Friday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; after hours, weekends and closures call and press 2 for a licensed clinician

wayne-state-university-counseling-and-ps.d: Counseling and a free mental health assessment for currently enrolled Wayne State students, with a 24-hour phone line outside office hours.
wayne-state-university-counseling-and-ps.hours: Office Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.; at all other times and during closures call 313-577-CAPS (2277)

university-of-detroit-mercy-wellness-cen.d: Personal counseling with Michigan-licensed clinicians for University of Detroit Mercy students, requested through an online contact form or email.

michigan-crisis-and-access-line-mical-an.d: Free, confidential crisis counseling by call or text for anyone in Michigan in emotional distress, a mental health or substance use crisis, or worried about someone.

michigan-211.d: Free, confidential referrals to local help such as food, housing, bills and crisis support, by phone, text or chat. Open to anyone in Michigan.

detroit-wayne-integrated-health-network-.d: Free, confidential 24/7 crisis and support line for anyone in Wayne County facing a mental health or substance use emergency, with mobile crisis and walk-in options.

washtenaw-county-community-mental-health.d: Round-the-clock phone crisis line, mobile crisis team and suicide risk assessments for Washtenaw County residents with urgent needs.

oakland-community-health-network-ochn-cr.d: Crisis line for anyone in Oakland County in a suicidal, mental health or substance use crisis, with a separate mobile crisis unit for adults.

common-ground-crisis-hub.d: Free, confidential crisis support, 24/7 by phone, with text and chat through 988, for anyone seeking crisis help, run by a Michigan crisis agency.

macomb-county-community-mental-health-mc.d: Crisis line answered day and night for Macomb County residents in a mental health crisis, run by Macomb County Community Mental Health.
macomb-county-community-mental-health-mc.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

community-mental-health-authority-of-cli.d: 24/7 crisis triage, evaluation and screening for psychiatric emergencies for residents of Clinton, Eaton and Ingham counties, including the East Lansing area.

my-mental-wellness-helpline-islamic-cent.d: Free, anonymous after-hours peer listening line with faith-informed, culturally sensitive responders, run through Naseeha. Not a therapy or crisis line.
my-mental-wellness-helpline-islamic-cent.hours: Monday to Friday, 6 p.m. to 10 p.m.

my-mental-wellness-clinic-islamic-center.d: Free, faith-based and culturally guided therapy with licensed clinicians for children, teens, adults and elders, in person at the Islamic Center of Detroit or virtually.
my-mental-wellness-clinic-islamic-center.hours: Monday to Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

michigan-muslim-mental-health-directory-.d: A community-based directory developed by The Family & Youth Institute to connect Michigan Muslims with faith-sensitive therapists across the state.

icna-relief-michigan-muslim-family-servi.d: Free and low-cost social services, including refugee support, food aid, and limited mental health services tailored to the needs of Michigan's Muslim communities.

cognitive-care-center.d: Psychiatric evaluations, therapy, and medication management for children and adults, with providers experienced in treating clients from Muslim and minority backgrounds.
cognitive-care-center.hours: Monday to Saturday 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.; Sunday by appointment

arab-community-center-for-economic-and-s.d: Counseling, psychiatric services, case management and peer support for adults, children and families in Southeast Michigan, including Arab American and immigrant communities.

chaldean-community-foundation-project-li.d: Mental health screening, consultation and therapy from licensed trilingual therapists for Michigan residents aged 13 and up, regardless of insurance status.

988-suicide-crisis-lifeline.d: Call, text or chat with a trained crisis counselor about suicidal thoughts, emotional distress or any mental health crisis.
988-suicide-crisis-lifeline.languages: English and Spanish (site states text and chat are available in Spanish)

crisis-text-line.d: Text with a volunteer crisis counselor for support during a crisis or any hard moment.

samhsa-national-helpline.d: Treatment referral and information service for mental health conditions and substance use, for individuals and families.
samhsa-national-helpline.languages: English and Spanish by phone; text service is English only

naseeha-mental-health-helpline.d: Free peer support helpline run by Naseeha, open around the clock for people who want someone to talk to.

the-trevor-project.d: Crisis counselors reachable by phone, text or online chat for LGBTQ+ young people.

veterans-crisis-line.d: Confidential support by phone, text or chat for veterans, service members and their families in crisis.

stronghearts-native-helpline.d: Confidential helpline for Native Americans and Alaska Natives affected by domestic, dating or sexual violence.

disaster-distress-helpline.d: Crisis counseling by phone or text for people distressed by a disaster, including natural and human-caused events.
disaster-distress-helpline.cost: Free (toll-free; standard text rates may apply)
disaster-distress-helpline.languages: Over 100 languages via interpretation; Spanish: press 2

trans-lifeline.d: Peer support hotline for trans and questioning people, answered by phone on weekdays.
trans-lifeline.hours: Monday to Friday, 1 PM to 9 PM Eastern (10 AM to 6 PM Pacific)

muslim-therapist-directory.d: An online platform that connects individuals with licensed Muslim mental health professionals across various regions.

institute-for-muslim-mental-health.d: Research, training and resources on Muslim American mental health, with a link to the Muslim Therapist Directory.

maristan.d: A collection of mental health tools, articles, and educational materials designed to support Muslim communities through spiritually integrated care and culturally sensitive guidance.

khalil-center.d: Clinical services integrating Islamic spirituality and psychology. Offers individual therapy, workshops, and training for professionals.
khalil-center.cost: Insurance accepted; sliding scale financial assistance

ruh-care.d: Online therapy by phone or video with licensed Muslim therapists, for individuals, couples, children and families.
ruh-care.cost: $120 to $200 per session; sliding scale assistance for those without insurance
ruh-care.languages: ASL, Arabic, Bangla, Creole, English, Farsi, French, German, Harari, Hindi, Malayalam, Pashto, Punjabi, Rohingya, Sindhi, Somali, Tamil, Urdu, Wolof

the-family-youth-institute.d: National nonprofit offering a resource hub on Muslim American mental health, covering stigma, suicide, grief, therapy, parenting and youth.

muslim-mental-health-and-islamic-psychol.d: Stanford Medicine research lab publishing studies, suicide response guidance and trainings on Islamic psychology and Muslim mental health.

muslim-mental-health-consortium-michigan.d: Hosts the annual Muslim Mental Health Conference and related resources for practitioners, faith leaders and community members.

black-mental-health-alliance.d: Education, training, and resources to support mental wellness in Black communities, including a therapist referral service.

beam.d: Healing, training, and peer support for Black individuals and families with a trauma-informed, community-centered approach.

therapy-for-black-girls.d: Directory of culturally responsive therapists at providers.therapyforblackgirls.com, plus a podcast and blog.

latinx-therapy.d: Bilingual therapy directories, podcast episodes, and resources aimed at dismantling mental health stigma in Latinx communities.
latinx-therapy.cost: Sliding scale and private pay (varies by provider)
latinx-therapy.languages: English and Spanish; some providers also Spanglish

asian-mental-health-collective.d: A therapist directory and mental health resources designed to make care more accessible for Asian and Pacific Islander individuals.
asian-mental-health-collective.cost: Therapy Fund is free (16 sessions over six months, by application); directory cost not stated

south-asian-mental-health-initiative-and.d: Non-emergency helpline, support groups and a provider directory for South Asian communities in the US.

the-steve-fund.d: Supports the mental health and emotional well-being of young people of color through campus programs, research, and crisis support.

we-r-native.d: Health and wellness resource for Native youth, with articles, an Ask Your Relative question service and text message programs.

national-queer-and-trans-therapists-of-c.d: National directory of queer and trans therapists of color, plus a practitioner membership program and community resources.

open-path-collective.d: Directory of therapists offering reduced-rate sessions to members who pay a one-time membership fee.
open-path-collective.cost: Low-cost sessions set by therapist plus a one-time membership fee

psychology-today-therapist-finder.d: Searchable directory of therapists by location, concern and specialty.

rainn-national-sexual-assault-hotline.d: Talk by phone, text or online chat with a trained staff member who supports survivors of sexual violence and their loved ones.

1in6.d: Free, counselor-facilitated text-based online support groups for men 18 and older who experienced sexual abuse or assault. Peer support, not therapy or crisis service.
1in6.hours: Weekly online sessions, about 1 hour each, several evenings and one midday per week (Eastern and Pacific times listed on site)

dod-safe-helpline.d: Support by phone and online chat for members of the Department of Defense community and their loved ones affected by sexual assault.

national-domestic-violence-hotline.d: Call, text or chat with an advocate about domestic violence, safety planning and local resources.
national-domestic-violence-hotline.languages: English and Spanish (Spanish site at espanol.thehotline.org)

national-domestic-violence-hotline-deaf-.d: A videophone line for Deaf and hard of hearing people to reach an advocate about domestic violence.

love-is-respect.d: Phone, text and live chat support for teens and young adults about dating abuse and unhealthy relationships, plus information for friends and family.

peaceful-families-project.d: A Muslim-focused nonprofit offering domestic violence toolkits and a directory that connects survivors with domestic violence organizations and shelters across the US and Canada.

heart-health-education-advocacy-research.d: A Chicago-based nonprofit offering faith-informed sexual health and violence education and a Get Support section for Muslim communities.

tahirih-justice-center.d: Free legal services and case management for immigrant women, girls and survivors of gender-based violence, with offices in VA, GA, MD, TX and CA.

esperanza-united.d: A national resource center for Latin@ communities with a directory of national and local organizations and guides on domestic and sexual violence.

womenslaw-org-email-hotline.d: Free-to-read US legal information on domestic violence, sexual assault and stalking, with an email hotline answered by attorneys. It gives legal information, not legal advice.

national-human-trafficking-hotline.d: Confidential phone, text and chat help for victims and survivors of human trafficking and people who suspect trafficking.

childhelp-national-child-abuse-hotline.d: Phone, text and chat with a counselor for children, teens and adults concerned about child abuse. It is not a reporting line.

national-runaway-safeline.d: Crisis support by phone, text and chat for youth who are thinking of running away or are homeless, and for their families.

boys-town-national-hotline.d: Counselors answer calls and texts from kids, teens and parents about crisis, family conflict, abuse and other concerns.
boys-town-national-hotline.hours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
boys-town-national-hotline.languages: English; Spanish-speaking counselors; translation for more than 100 languages

youthline.d: Free peer-to-peer support, help and crisis line for youth up to age 24, by phone, text, chat or email.
youthline.hours: Youth volunteers daily 4 to 10 PM Pacific; adults staff the phone at other times
youthline.languages: English; live interpreter available on phone calls

eldercare-locator.d: A federal service that connects older adults and caregivers with local aging services, including help with elder abuse and caregiving.

partnership-to-end-addiction-helpline.d: Parents and families can call, text or email a specialist to get help for a child or loved one struggling with substance use.

alcoholics-anonymous-find-a-meeting.d: Find in-person A.A. meetings through the Meeting Guide app or local A.A. resources, and online meetings through the Online Intergroup.

narcotics-anonymous-meeting-search.d: Find in-person NA meetings through local NA communities and online meetings through the Virtual Meeting Finder, or use the free meeting search app.

millati-islami.d: A twelve-step recovery fellowship grounded in Islamic principles, with in-person meetings in major cities, Zoom meetings most days, and a telephone meeting.

anad-eating-disorders-helpline.d: A free helpline offering emotional support and referrals for people affected by eating disorders. Messages left outside open hours are returned.
anad-eating-disorders-helpline.hours: Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 9 PM Central

national-alliance-for-eating-disorders-h.d: A free helpline for people with eating disorders and their families, with referrals to treatment and support.
national-alliance-for-eating-disorders-h.hours: 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM Eastern, Monday to Friday

national-maternal-mental-health-hotline.d: Free confidential support by call or text for pregnant and postpartum people and their families, answered by trained counselors and peer specialists.
national-maternal-mental-health-hotline.languages: English and Spanish; interpreters for over 60 languages

postpartum-support-international-helplin.d: Volunteers return calls and texts with support, information and referrals for perinatal mood and anxiety concerns. It is not a crisis line.
postpartum-support-international-helplin.hours: Leave a message anytime; volunteers return calls and texts daily, 8 AM to 11 PM Eastern

the-dougy-center.d: Free grief toolkits and education for grieving children, teens and families, plus a worldwide directory of peer grief support programs.

the-compassionate-friends.d: Grief support for families after the death of a child at any age, through more than 500 local chapters and online groups.

american-foundation-for-suicide-preventi.d: Support for people bereaved by suicide, including Healing Conversations with trained survivor volunteers, a support group directory, guides and a clinician directory.
american-foundation-for-suicide-preventi.languages: English and Spanish (Surviving a Suicide Loss booklet)

alliance-of-hope-for-suicide-loss-surviv.d: An online forum and resources for people who have lost someone to suicide, with a supportive community of other survivors.

cdc-caring-for-your-mental-health.d: A CDC page with tips and links for crisis support, finding providers, peer support, basic needs and hotlines for violence, abuse and trafficking.

nimh-help-for-mental-illnesses.d: Guidance on getting immediate help, finding a provider or treatment, judging whether a provider is a good fit, and learning about mental disorders.

nami-helpline.d: Trained staff and volunteers offer information, referrals and support for people with mental health conditions and their families. It is not a crisis line.
nami-helpline.hours: Monday to Friday, 10 AM to 10 PM Eastern

mental-health-america-screening-tools.d: Free, anonymous online screening tests for depression, anxiety, PTSD and other conditions, with next-step resources. Results are not a diagnosis.

findtreatment-gov.d: SAMHSA's locator for mental health and substance use treatment facilities, filterable by location, services and payment accepted.

hrsa-find-a-health-center.d: A federal tool to find health centers that give primary and often behavioral health care, with fees scaled to income whether or not you have insurance.
hrsa-find-a-health-center.cost: Sliding fee based on ability to pay

warmline-org-directory.d: A state-by-state directory of peer-run warmlines, where you can talk with someone before a situation becomes a crisis. Some lines accept calls nationwide.

inclusive-therapists.d: A nationwide directory centering BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and neurodivergent therapists, with filters for cultural, spiritual, and language-based needs.
